title: Restoring Electricity
description: From 'what is energy?' to a small, safe off-grid DC power system. A curated dependency graph: each node lists what you must understand first.

nodes.title: Energy & power
nodes.summary: Energy is the capacity to do work; power is how fast it's used (watts). Every rebuilding decision is an energy budget.
nodes.why: You can't plan electricity without knowing how much energy you have and how much you need.

safety.note: Pure theory — safe to learn anywhere.

goals: Explain the difference between energy (Wh) and power (W)
Estimate a torch's daily energy use
nodes.activity: Read the label on three devices and write down their watts or milliamp-hours.

nodes.title: Charge & current
nodes.summary: Electric current is the flow of charge through a conductor, driven by a difference in electric potential.
nodes.why: Everything electrical — from a torch to a power grid — is controlled charge flow.
goals: Describe conductors vs. insulators
Explain AC vs. DC in one sentence
nodes.activity: Explore the PhET Circuit Construction Kit simulation (download it while you still have internet).

nodes.title: Electrical safety
nodes.summary: How shocks, burns and electrical fires happen, and the rules that prevent them.
nodes.why: Mistakes with electricity can be fatal. Safety is a prerequisite for every hands-on node.

safety.note: Mains wiring and fixed installations must be done by licensed electricians.

goals: List three mains-electricity hazards
Know why back-feeding a house is lethal
Know who to call for fixed wiring
nodes.activity: Find your home's switchboard and identify (don't open) the main switch and safety switches (RCDs).

nodes.title: Voltage, current & resistance
nodes.summary: Ohm's law (V = I × R) and power (P = V × I) let you predict how circuits behave.
nodes.why: Lets you size wires, fuses and batteries instead of guessing.

safety.note: Practise with AA/AAA batteries and simulations only.

goals: Calculate current from voltage and resistance
Calculate power of a 12 V, 2 A load
nodes.activity: Simulate a bulb with 1, 2 and 3 batteries in PhET and record what changes.

nodes.title: Simple circuits
nodes.summary: Series and parallel circuits, switches and fuses at low (battery) voltage.
nodes.why: Circuits are the building blocks of every lighting or charging setup.

safety.note: Low-voltage (≤12 V) battery circuits only. Never connect experiments to mains.

goals: Build a series and a parallel LED circuit with a commercial kit
Explain what a fuse protects
nodes.activity: With a certified low-voltage kit, light one LED, then two in parallel.

nodes.title: Magnetism & induction
nodes.summary: Moving a magnet near a coil induces a current — the principle behind every generator and alternator.
nodes.why: It's how mechanical energy (wind, water, muscle) becomes electricity.
goals: Explain Faraday's law of induction in plain words
Describe how a hand-crank radio charges
nodes.activity: Use a wind-up radio or torch and notice how cranking speed changes brightness.

nodes.title: Mechanical generation
nodes.summary: Generators and alternators convert motion into electricity: hand-crank, bicycle, wind and water.
nodes.why: Generation independent of the grid and of fuel supply.

safety.note: Use certified products. Fuel generators: outdoors only (carbon monoxide). Never connect to house wiring without a licensed electrician.

goals: Compare hand-crank vs. fuel generator energy output
Explain why fuel generators must stay outside
nodes.activity: Time how long cranking a wind-up radio for one minute keeps it running.

nodes.title: Load & energy budgeting
nodes.summary: List every device, its watts and hours of use, and total the watt-hours per day.
nodes.why: Tells you what size of solar panel and battery you actually need — and what to switch off.
goals: Write your household's essential daily Wh budget
Rank loads: critical, useful, luxury
nodes.activity: Budget: 2 LED torches (1 W × 4 h), radio (2 W × 3 h), 2 phones (10 Wh each) — total it.

nodes.title: Batteries & storage
nodes.summary: Chemical storage of electrical energy: capacity (Wh), chemistry, charge/discharge and hazards.
nodes.why: Solar and wind are intermittent. Storage lets you use energy when you need it.

safety.note: Never short-circuit, puncture or overheat batteries. Swollen lithium cells are a fire risk.

goals: Estimate runtime: Wh ÷ W
Explain why lithium batteries need protection circuits
nodes.activity: Read the Wh rating on a power bank and estimate how many phone charges it holds.

nodes.title: Solar photovoltaics
nodes.summary: PV panels convert sunlight directly into DC electricity. Output varies with sun, angle, heat and shade.
nodes.why: The most accessible off-grid generation for a household: no fuel, few moving parts.

safety.note: Panels produce voltage whenever lit. Use certified portable kits; roof systems need licensed installers.

goals: Estimate daily Wh from a panel's watt rating and sun hours
Explain the effect of shading
nodes.activity: Charge a power bank from a small solar charger in morning vs. midday sun and compare.

nodes.title: Solar charging & storage
nodes.summary: Charge controllers, batteries and inverters: how solar energy is stored and used safely.
nodes.why: Turns daytime sunlight into night-time light and communications.

safety.note: Use integrated, certified portable power stations. Building DIY battery banks or connecting to house wiring requires qualified professionals.

goals: Explain what a charge controller does
Match a power station's Wh to your energy budget
nodes.activity: Compare two certified portable power stations by Wh capacity, output ports and solar input watts.

nodes.title: Small off-grid DC power
nodes.summary: A safe household setup: solar panel + certified power station powering LED lights, radio and phone charging.
nodes.why: Restores the essentials — light, information, communication — without the grid.

safety.note: Stay with plug-and-play certified equipment. Anything wired into the building is a job for a licensed electrician.

goals: Design (on paper) a system meeting your essential Wh budget
Plan maintenance and safe storage
nodes.activity: Write your household's off-grid essentials plan: loads, Wh per day, equipment you have, equipment missing.
